Specifically:
  - Does the 72h window include KMS key material movement?
  - Are audit logs and telemetry guaranteed to remain in-region (or at least masked) during the window?

We attached our standard compliance attachment to show what our GC is looking for. Let me know if you prefer a short call.

Alyssa / Vanessa / Laura —

Technical clarifications from infra/ops perspective (short bullets):

- Region affinity: We pin compute and primary storage to the customer's chosen region (EU) using region-scoped routing and placement constraints. Metadata and control-plane signals may touch other regions for orchestration but are not arbitrarily processed outside EU.

- Default transient window: Our production baseline is 48h for unplanned failover replication. For enterprise addenda we can support a 72h transit exception under these conditional controls:
  1) Trigger criteria: failover only after primary-region unavailability detection and runbook execution (alert + operator ack).
  2) Notification: Redwood will notify the customer and the DPO within 30 minutes of initiation and provide hourly status updates until data is restored.
  3) Telemetry/audit logs: logs that contain customer PII are masked in transit; full audit logs are written to region-backed archival storage; streaming telemetry used for failover may traverse control-plane regions but we will provide signed attestations and retention timestamps.
  4) KMS policy: Primary keys remain region-bound. For the 72h exception we offer a controlled-wrap model: ephemeral wrapping keys can be provisioned in a secondary region under an escrowed policy. Key movement requires dual-operator approval and is logged.
  5) Subprocessors: any out-of-region processing (even transient) involving subprocessors will be listed in an annex and customers will get advance notice on scheduled maintenance; emergency failover roster entries will be provided post-incident.

- Evidence & auditability: We can provide (a) a snapshot of subprocessor roster (attached), (b) last SOC2 summary and controls mapping on telemetry residency, and (c) a sample affidavit language for legal.

I'll add formal operational runbook language to the draft affidavit (Vanessa: see the comments I added in the Drive link).

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Serving Operations, Redwood Inference
